items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: I stayed in the band about three years... Jimmy Archey was asked to take charge of the band, to go into Jimmy Ryan's... So then I joined the band.

ctx.x: So you were willing to go the route -

My vision, I mean New York City is a big thing, you know what I'm saying, you know what I mean, you know? Like the same thing with - look, with the same thing in Paris. When I left here, I didn't go to Paris with Jimmy Archey.

items.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: A visit to Europe with Jimmy Archey led to a stay of almost 40 years

ctx.x: Benny Waters lays claim to be the oldest working jazzman in the country, probably in the world. Born in Maryland in 1902, Benny showed an early musical aptitude, giving piano recitals by age seven, and soon after learning the reed instruments from his older brother. He played in dance bands while still in high school and attended the Boston Conservatory of Music where he studied piano and theory while teaching clarinet.
